html:
The Tajikistani civil war was fought from 1992 to 1997 between the post-Soviet government of Tajikistan and an opposition of Islamists, democrats and regional groups from Garm and the Pamirs.

After independence, power struggles between regions turned to war. Militias from Kulob and Khujand, backed by Russia and Uzbekistan, took Dushanbe in late 1992, and Emomali Rahmon became head of state. Opposition fighters fled to Afghanistan and fought on from there. Tens of thousands died, perhaps many more, and hundreds of thousands fled.

A peace deal in 1997, brokered by the United Nations, Russia and Iran, gave the opposition a share of posts. Rahmon slowly squeezed them out and banned the Islamic party in 2015. Fear of another war long kept Tajiks from challenging him.
sum: The Tajikistani civil war was fought from 1992 to 1997 between the post-Soviet government of Tajikistan and an opposition of Islamists, democrats and regional groups from Garm and the Pamirs.
